stem: On the number line, mark every integer $n$ from $-3$ to $3$ for which $\dfrac{n-2}{n}$ is undefined. Leave the other integers unmarked.
solution: A fraction is undefined exactly when its denominator is zero. The top of the fraction plays no part in that test.
The denominator is $n$, which is zero only when $n = 0$. Then the fraction is $\dfrac{-2}{0}$, which is undefined. Mark $0$.

Check the tempting value: the top, $n - 2$, is zero when $n = 2$. Then $\dfrac{n-2}{n} = \dfrac{0}{2} = 0$, a perfectly good real number, because a zero on top is not division by zero. Leave $2$ unmarked.
Every other integer from $-3$ to $3$ gives a non-zero denominator and a real value. The marked set is $\{0\}$.
notes: Fit: the zero on top and the zero on the bottom are placed at different points of the same line (n = 2 and n = 0), so the student has to decide which zero makes the fraction undefined; that is the exact contrast between the book's $\dfrac{0}{\sqrt{2}}$ (real) and $\dfrac{-\sqrt{7}}{0}$ (undefined). Same family-of-integers caveat as the other template. The denominator is plain $n$ on purpose: a denominator like $n - 2$ would add a sign-flip trap (marking -2 for $n - 2 = 0$) that belongs to solving equations, not to this objective. With one target, a student who judges by the top marks {2}, which fires missed-values (and extra-values); one who also marks the right value gives {0, 2}, which fires extra-values only. Both predicates are mapped to the same misconception because the only attractive wrong value on this line is the zero-on-top one; a stray tap elsewhere would be misdiagnosed, which is accepted as unlikely. sign-flipped cannot fire (the answer set equals its own negation). non-real-undefined-swapped is not visible here. Single fixed question, no instances.
